5.3 SIF

For the current problem, we do not have an asymptotic or analytical solution. Therefore, an explicit description of crack-tip SIF is not available. However, one can utilize the crack-tip SIF defined for the linear elastic fracture mechanics model and use the finite element solution for the nonlinear model to glean some vital physical insight into SIF.

0.0037, 0.0026 (Unit: 10⅔mm /2Pa). All the Ky values are very close, implying an identical theoretical Ky value for all B is highly likely. Such numerical approximation for Ky shows that the nonlinear model with density-dependent moduli is designed appropriately under the common crack criteria used for the linear-elasticity fracture model. Also, in the two panels of Fig. 7, the curve shapes for 8 < 0 and ß > 0 are slightly distinct. The B < 0 curves show a greater curvature, while those for 3 > 0 show flatter behaviors. Such difference is caused by the sign of B, disclosing how negative and positive & values impact the SIF differently.
